harness.api:
Import from the repository root with `uv run python` (export TMPDIR=<tmp> CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" OMP_NUM_THREADS<=3; the harness sets no thread limits itself):
    import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "diagnosis/probe_capacity"); import harness as h
The harness puts diagnosis/probe_metrics on sys.path itself and exposes the frozen reading module as h.nr (nolly_reading).

CONSTANTS
- h.FS = 48000. h.SKIP = 2400: samples left unscored at the start of every read section. h.FLOOR = 1e-4 (Protocol.floor). h.WINDOW = 2400 (50 ms).
- h.FIT = "di_train" (A, 5,760,000 samples at 48 kHz); h.VALID = "di_validation" (V, 1,440,000); h.READ = "di_test" (B, 1,440,000). Rule: B never enters a fit. Select on V (read=h.VALID), then report B once. Label anything fitted on B as an oracle.
- h.SECTIONS: the 19 cached names: di_train, di_validation, di_test, pink_noise_-30dBFS_rms, multisine_{-30,-24,-18}dBFS_rms_r{1..4} (12 sections), steps_{-30,-24,-18}dBFS_rms. Every section is cut at its 192 kHz layout offset with no latency advance, then decimated by 4 on its own with nr.dec, exactly as the frozen reading does. Layout metadata is at 192 kHz: h.nr.SECTIONS[name]["onsets"] and ["period_samples"] must be divided by 4 for the cached arrays (multisine period = 48000 samples at 48 kHz, 3 periods, the first one transient).
- h.ROWS: {take: settings.csv row as str fields: order, block, G, B, M, T, P, cab, split, setting, file}, takes 1..42.
- h.USABLE: the 34 takes that passed gate 4. h.EXCLUDED = (9, 12, 13, 18, 23, 24, 38, 41), which failed gate 4 (marker lags); usable for capacity studies, but say so when you use them.
- h.GAIN_TAKES = {0.0: 30, 2.5: 16, 5.0: 20, 7.5: 6, 10.0: 7}, the H2 ladder.
- h.FROZEN: {name: frozen spec}: "fir" (FIR 256 taps, ridge 1e-2), "hammerstein_3" and "hammerstein_5" (256 taps, ridge 1e-4), "volterra_laguerre_2" (8 Laguerre, pole 0.8, ridge 1e-4), "volterra_laguerre_3" (8 Laguerre, pole 0.9, ridge 1e-4). Built from dev_select.json and dev_select_v2.json through calibrate.frozen_probes.
- h.READING: the parsed diagnosis/probe_metrics/nolly_reading.json. h.CACHE: the cache Path.

DATA
- h.load(take: int | "x", names=(h.FIT, h.READ)) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]: cached 48 kHz sections, as read-only float64 memmaps (in-place edits raise an error).
- h.section_inputs(section: str, ref: int | None = None) -> dict: {"x": source section}, plus "y_ref": the output of take `ref` on the same section, only when ref is given.
- h.difference(ref: int, eval_take: int, section: str) -> np.ndarray: y_eval - y_ref.
- h.build(jobs=3): already run; it skips tags whose 19 files are already present.

PROBES
- h.CapacityProbe (typing.Protocol): fit(inputs: dict[str, ndarray], target: ndarray) -> self; predict(inputs: dict) -> ndarray, same length as inputs["x"]. A probe only ever receives the inputs dict and the target on the fit section, never the target on the read section.
- h.FrozenProbe(name: str): one of h.FROZEN, fitted and rendered with fssr_nam.product.probes.fit_probe and the sum of probe_contributions, exactly as analyze_pair does. It uses inputs["x"] only.
- h.FeatureProbe(features: Callable[[dict], list[ndarray]], taps: int = 256, ridge: float = 1e-4): q = c + sum_k h_k * (f_k / s_k). Each feature has its own causal FIR of `taps` taps; s_k is the RMS of f_k on the fit section's inputs; the ridge is relative to the mean Gram diagonal (probes.normal_equations/regularized). It stays linear in the target as long as `features` never reads the target (features may use x and y_ref). Check: features [x**1..x**5] reproduce Hammerstein 5 exactly (0.8056428222917209 on take 2 for both). Output-referenced example: FeatureProbe(lambda i: [i["y_ref"]]).

METRICS (fit, read: any name in h.SECTIONS; defaults fit=h.FIT, read=h.READ)
- h.ratio(y, q, floor=h.FLOOR) -> float: RMS((y-q)[SKIP:]) / max(RMS(y[SKIP:]), floor).
- h.fit_read(probe, target_a, ref=None, fit=FIT, read=READ) -> ndarray: fits on (section_inputs(fit, ref), target_a) and returns the prediction on `read`.
- h.output_capacity(probe, take, ref=None, fit=FIT, read=READ) -> float: residual / RMS of the take's own output on `read`, with the 1e-4 floor. This is the frozen capacity_eval. With ref, the probe also receives that take's output as y_ref. ORACLE TRAP: ref == take, or a ref close to it, with a y_ref-fed probe is trivially near 0. Any y_ref-fed probe makes the frozen bound's r_ref vacuous, so label such runs.
- h.level_capacity_from(x, y, q, bins=5) -> list[dict]: per bin {"input_db": [lo, hi], "windows": n, "output_db": RMS of y in dBFS, "capacity": rms(y-q)/max(rms(y), FLOOR)}. Non-overlapping 50 ms windows of x after SKIP (the partial last window is dropped), in equal-count bins on the quantiles of the windows' input RMS. The edges depend on x only, so they are the same for every take on a given section and differ between sections.
- h.level_capacity(probe, take, ref=None, bins=5, fit=FIT, read=READ) -> list[dict]: the same, after fitting.
- h.difference_share(probe, ref, eval_take, fit=FIT, read=READ) -> float: RMS(d_B - q_B) / RMS(d_B) with d = y_eval - y_ref, the probe fitted on d_A with inputs {x, y_ref = ref's output}. NO floor, so it equals the frozen unrepresented / d_audio.
- h.linearity_check(probe, ref, eval_take, fit=FIT, read=READ) -> float: RMS(fit(y_eval) - fit(y_ref) - fit(d)) / RMS(fit(d)) on read after SKIP, the three fits on the same inputs {x, y_ref}. About 1e-12 when the probe is linear in the target. It costs 3 fits.
- h.frozen_prediction(name, take, ref=None, read=READ) -> ndarray (memmap): prediction of frozen probe `name` fitted on A to the take's output (ref None) or to take - ref. Computed and cached when missing. Cached already: every take 1..42 and the 20 one-knob differences, on di_test, for the 5 probes. A new request (e.g. read=VALID) costs one fit (VL3 about 50 s). The cache is keyed by name/take/section only.

PAIRS
- h.pairs(kinds: tuple[str, ...] | None = None, excluded: bool = False) -> list[dict{ref, eval, kind, excluded}]: exactly the 34 pairs of nolly_reading.json (kinds "repeat", "one_knob", "combination_test", "combination_train", "cab"). excluded=True adds the 8 pairs of nr.pairs() that involve an EXCLUDED take, flagged excluded=True. kinds must be a tuple, e.g. h.pairs(("one_knob",)). One-knob: 19 listed, plus (20, 23) flagged.
- h.knob(pair) -> "G" | "B" | "M" | "T" | "P": the knob a one-knob pair moves (one-knob pairs only).

CLI: `uv run python diagnosis/probe_capacity/harness.py build` (the cache, 3 processes) and `... baseline [--jobs 3]` (writes diagnosis/probe_capacity/baseline.json; about 6 s now that the predictions are cached). baseline.json has keys protocol, excluded_takes_gate4, gain_takes, probes[name]{version, capacity_by_gain, capacity_by_level (the 5 gains, 5 bins), capacity_by_take{take: {value, excluded}}, difference_share_one_knob[{ref, eval, kind, excluded, knob, setting, share_from_x, frozen_share, linearity_gap}]}, instrument_check.
Measured timings, fit on A plus predict on B: H5 8 s and VL3 47 s at 3 threads; FeatureProbe with 5 features x 256 taps 8 s.

Status: the harness is in place, the cache is built (43 tags x 19 sections), baseline.json is written, the instrument check matches to about 1e-15, and ruff check and format are clean. Only these were written: diagnosis/probe_capacity/harness.py, diagnosis/probe_capacity/baseline.json, and the gitignored diagnosis/probe_capacity/__pycache__/. Plus tmp/probe_capacity/ (cache, predictions, logs) and one smoke script in the session scratchpad (nl_research/harness_smoke.py). No git command that changes state was run. The .pyc files in probe_metrics/__pycache__ predate this session. Every process I started has exited; the GPU queue was not touched.

Additions beyond the request (stated, not hidden):
1. di_validation (V) is cached so the leads can select hyper-parameters without reading B. The frozen reading never used V.
2. Capacity was also computed for the 8 gate-4 takes, flagged excluded, and the one-knob pair (20, 23) has a difference share, flagged.
3. The instrument check was extended to all 5 probes x 34 takes, to the difference shares of the 19 pairs, and to linearity in y.
4. frozen_prediction caches the frozen predictions on B, so leads can study residuals cheaply.
5. FeatureProbe is a generic plug-in probe with frozen features, taken from the scratch study's Model.

Codex review (gpt-6-astra, xhigh, read-only, no computation), 6 findings at P2. Fixed:
- (1) difference_share divided by max(RMS(d), 1e-4) where the frozen unrepresented / d_audio uses plain RMS(d). It now uses floor 0. The values on these pairs do not change, since RMS(d) is far above 1e-4.
- (2) The pass flag only covered H2. It now also requires the capacity gap, the share gap and linearity; pass_H2 is reported separately.
- (3) Temporary file names could collide. They now carry a uuid suffix.

Declined, with the reasons:
- (4) Prediction cache not keyed by data version: the probes are frozen and the sections are built once. This is documented in the docstring: delete frozen_pred/ if the sections are rebuilt.
- (5) Division by zero when RMS(fit(d)) = 0: only happens for identical takes.
- (6) Empty bins when window levels are tied: x_B has no tied windows (its quietest window is -75.3 dBFS); an empty bin returns NaN with windows = 0.
baseline.json was regenerated with the fixed code from the cached predictions; the numbers are unchanged.

Measurements the leads can use (established, from baseline.json):
(a) Residual by input level. At G >= 2.5, the H5 and VL3 residual share is largest in the quietest input quintile (0.88-0.90) and smallest in the 4th quintile (0.65-0.74). At G0 it is flat, 0.41-0.50.
(b) Output level by input level. At G >= 2.5 the output RMS stays within about 1.4 dB (-19.1 to -17.4 dBFS) while the input quintiles span about -28 to -12 dBFS. At G0 the output spans -31.0 to -21.6 dBFS.
(c) Differences from x. The difference share from x is 0.76-0.95 for the tone knobs and 0.90-0.99 for the gain pairs (H5 / VL3), and VL3 is not uniformly better than H5 there (B pairs: 0.886 vs 0.829).

Supposed, not tested: (a) and (b) are consistent with a level-dependent gain or dynamic compression that a static polynomial with 256-tap memory cannot carry. The quiet-input windows may also hold the decay tails of loud notes. No discriminating test has been run yet; this is for lead 4.

Caveats for the leads:
- Any y_ref-fed probe must be labelled. Its frozen-bound r_ref is vacuous, and ref == take is an oracle.
- The harness does not limit threads. Callers export OMP_NUM_THREADS and keep at most 3 threads or processes in total.
- Import cost: about 1 s (nolly_reading.json, 466 KB, is parsed on import).

leads.mechanism:
Established (checks stage): when y_ref is a feature and its FIR can carry the identity, the residual of fitting d equals the residual of fitting y_eval with the same features. r_eval / unrepresented = 0.9986 to 1.0003 on 7 non-repeat pairs. So the probe of the change is a conditional, transmissibility-like model of y_eval given y_ref (and x); only the normalisation differs. Its fit of y_ref is near exact: r_ref/RMS(y_ref) = 2.2e-4 (yfir) and 8.3e-4 to 9.2e-4 (x5_yh5). The frozen bound |d_audio - d_probe| <= r_ref + r_eval therefore reduces to the triangle inequality with r_eval: the bound holds, r_ref is at most 6.8 % of the limit on non-repeat pairs, and it is vacuous.

What the probe captures (established, Nolly B, medians):
- A change that is a linear filter after everything (cabinet) is almost fully represented once the memory is long enough: 0.154 left with FIR 256, 0.046 with FIR 1024.
- Tone knobs leave 0.359 (FIR 256 on y_ref) and 0.264 to 0.267 (nonlinear y_ref features), against 0.829 for H5 from x.
- Gain changes leave 0.653 to 0.683, against 0.933 for H5.
- The residual is nearly flat across input-level quintiles (tone 0.23 to 0.32, gain 0.62 to 0.70); H5 is not flat.

Supposed: part of the tone change sits before, or interacts with, a nonlinearity. Two observations point that way: nonlinear y_ref features help on tone pairs (0.359 to 0.267) but not on gain pairs (0.681 to 0.678), and the tone residual is highest in the loudest input quintile (0.32 against 0.23 mid). Gain changes reshape the distortion itself, which no fixed function of a neighbouring output carries.
leads.fragile_hypothesis: The output-referenced probe works only when the change acts after the main clipping (tone knobs, cabinet) and fails for a gain change (before clipping). Secondary, pre-registered: for gain pairs, nonlinear y_ref features help more when the reference has the LOWER gain (re-clipping is possible, un-clipping is not).
leads.discriminating_observation:
VS100R model against device, defect unknown to the probe. Probes were fitted on di_validation and read on di_test, on 4 test takes (3, 16, 30, 36), with 3 seeds per arm, on CPU.

- **Arm C (SSM-WaveNet FiLM).** The x probes leave 0.95 to 0.98 of the model error. The output-referenced FIR leaves 0.365 (ref = model) and 0.345 (ref = device with 16 lead taps). The causal ref = device FIR leaves 0.640. That asymmetry flags a timing defect: the model output is early. An independent cross-correlation on V gives -1.11 samples (C early), consistent with tau +1.0 in evaluation_dry.json. Take 16, the unseen gain-contour pair, stays high at 0.545 to 0.618, against 0.235 to 0.447 on the other takes: a wrong knob response, not a filter.
- **Grey boxes.** GREY leaves 0.58 to 0.77 and L leaves 0.75 to 0.83 in either direction: structural errors, not filters.
- **F3 (not predicted).** The probe exposed an unknown lag on seeds 42 and 44: ref = model FIR leaves 0.834/0.578/0.905/0.772 (s42) and drops to 0.526/0.491/0.716/0.579 with lead taps. Cross-correlation on V then confirmed it: s42 is late by +2.0 samples, s44 by +3.6, and s43_r2 is early by 0.95.

So the referenced probe separates timing/EQ defects from structural ones where the x probes see nothing.

On Nolly, the discriminating split is tone against gain pairs. It includes the 10 combination pairs (2 with G unchanged, 8 with G changed) and the 15 tone pairs not seen in the scratch study. Controls: cab pairs (positive) and repeats (floor).

(1) The pre-registered primary rule is met. With the variant selected on V (x5_yh5), gain 0.653 >= 0.6, tone 0.267 <= 0.5 and the gap 0.386 >= 0.15, so the rule gives "supported"; FIR on y_ref alone also gives supported. Both controls behave as expected: cab 0.144 (0.046 with 1024 taps) and repeats 1.000.

(2) The pre-registered secondary prediction is refuted. Nonlinear y_ref features gain at most 0.022 over yfir on gain pairs, in either direction. The apparent direction asymmetry has two other causes. One is normalisation: RMS(d) against the output levels. In conditional capacity, 39->30 and 30->39 read 0.65 and 0.71 with yfir. The other is causality: 16 lead taps take 6->1 from 0.958 to 0.672. It is not clipping information loss.

(3) "Fails for gain" is too strong. On the same eval takes, conditional capacity is 0.415 against 0.771 for frozen H5, and the G7.5 neighbour leaves 0.310 against 0.800. At G0, though, the reference adds little: 0.398 against 0.476, and yfir alone is worse at 0.653.

(4) "Acts after the main clipping" is only partly right for tone knobs. Against the cab calibration (0.046), tone pairs stay at 0.264 even with yh5_1024, and nonlinear y_ref features help tone but not gain.

(5) On VS100R, the C predictions hold, as do the take-16 prediction and the grey-box threshold as written. The lead variant also revealed F3's lag, which was not predicted.
leads.leakage_and_controls:
**B never enters a fit.**
- Nolly probes are fitted on di_train. The variant is selected on di_validation (31 listed pairs; repeats, reversed pairs and gate-4 pairs excluded). B is then read once for every variant, all of which are reported.
- VS100R probes are fitted on di_validation and read on di_test. Nothing is selected on VS100R: the variant menu is the Nolly one. The VS100R timing check uses V only.
- Codex review (gpt-6-astra, xhigh, read-only) found no leakage, no causality or direction error, no class or selection-pool error, and a verdict implementation that matches its text. Its one P2 note: the conditional-capacity denominator uses the 1e-4 floor. I kept it because it matches the frozen capacity_eval it is compared with, and outputs are about 0.1 RMS, so it has no effect here.

**Linearity in y.** Measured for yfir and x5_yh5 on 8 pairs: at most 1.1e-12 on non-repeat pairs, 2.1e-8 on the repeat, where fit(d) is tiny. The other 6 variants have the same frozen-feature form (features never read the target), so they are linear by construction, but this was not measured.

**Oracles and labels.**
- Every variant is y_ref-fed, so the frozen bound's r_ref is vacuous (measured r_ref/RMS(y_ref) 2e-4 to 9e-4).
- Repeat pairs, and a conditional capacity whose reference has the same setting, are oracles. They are labelled, and gain 5 is not reported on the ladder.
- The conditional capacity is post hoc (computed after the B reading).

**Prediction timing.** The Nolly prediction was written after the scratch study had seen B with FIR 256 on y_ref for 6 pairs (1->2, 1->4, 1->7, 39->30, 39->35, 39->36). The VS100R prediction was written knowing evaluation_dry.json (C tau about +1, GREY about -0.5); both facts are stated in the JSON.

**Gate-4 takes** are used and flagged, in their own groups.

**Controls.**
- Instrument: frozen shares agree with nolly_reading.json to 2.4e-13.
- Positive control: the cab pairs.
- Floor: the repeats.
- Device noise floor on VS100R: at most 0.015 of the output (take 30), so at most about 0.07 of the C share there.
leads.limits:
- The probe needs a reference output for the same input: a nearby take or a model output. It is a fidelity and decomposition instrument, not an emulator. Conditional capacity depends on how close the reference is in knob space.
- The share is normalised by RMS(d), so it depends on direction and on the level ratio of the two outputs. Compare pairs with conditional capacity instead.
- Causal taps miss non-minimum-phase or advanced relations: reversed gain pairs, C, F3 s43. A y_ref window with lead taps is legitimate but was only tested as FIR (yfir_lead16), not combined with the nonlinear features.
- VS100R scope:
  - Only 4 of the 8 test takes.
  - F1 is absent (no record).
  - CPU fp32 inference, whereas the bench evaluation runs on GPU.
  - The scored region (SKIP 2400) is not the bench ESR window, so RMS(d)/RMS(y) is not the bench ESR.
  - The x probes fitted on V (1.44 M samples) give shares above 1 on several rows (VL3 up to 1.32): the model error does not generalise from V to B as a function of x.
- The VS100R lag comes from the cross-correlation peak, which mixes pure delay and phase. It is clean for C and F3, noisy for GREY (±1.5 between takes).
- Not run:
  - VL3 on y_ref (too costly).
  - Adjacent gain rungs (no frozen baseline).
  - VS100R device-against-device knob pairs (out of scope).
- Runtime was about 1 h 40 min of wall time at 3 threads/processes, over the hour guideline. Seeds 43 and 44 of C (about 15 min) could be dropped.
- Interpretations marked "supposed" (tone stack partly before a nonlinearity, F3 lag from the slow paths) have no discriminating test yet.

leads.mechanism:
ESTABLISHED (lead2_wh_gradient_frozen.json):
(1) The frozen probes are short on structure: their memory and degree are not the limit. Sandwiching static saturations between LEARNED filters, in a cascade, lowers the residual, and depth helps monotonically. Full-model residual on take 20, read on B (range over 3 seeds): 1 stage 0.382-0.395, 2 stages 0.298-0.342, 3 stages 0.260-0.287. Baselines: H5 0.803, scratch Wiener-BLA 0.748.
(2) Knob changes after the nonlinearity (tone stack, presence, cab on) are linear. The readout's per-feature FIRs absorb them, so features frozen from take 20 represent the other G5 takes at 0.236-0.29 (frozen-probe readings; H5 0.77-0.84 on the same takes).
(3) The gain knob changes the operating point inside the cascade. Transfer of frozen features loses more as the gain distance grows, and unevenly (transfer matrix). Scaling x before the frozen model does not recover it: the 5-drive bank gains only 0.02-0.04. Channels trained across the 5 gains do recover it (0.144-0.337 at the 5 gains), at a cost at G5 (0.307 against 0.258) with the same 8 channels.
(4) H5's quiet-input excess (0.88-0.90 in the quietest input-level fifth at G >= 2.5) is not slow dynamics. A static cascade with about 13 ms of total probe memory removes it: 3 x 127 channel-FIR samples (7.9 ms) plus 255 readout taps (5.3 ms).
SUPPOSED, not tested: the gain knob acts as an inter-stage drive inside the cascade rather than at its input. The per-take residual (0.09-0.30) is not decomposed: slow dynamics, the HF content or undertraining.
leads.fragile_hypothesis: That the gain knob is equivalent to a scaling of the input of a fixed nonlinear cascade. If it were, a frozen bank of the take-20 features evaluated at x*g, g in {0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4}, would approach the per-take models. Measured, it is REFUTED at the top of the range: G10 stays at 0.489 against 0.289 per take, and G0 at 0.297 against 0.094. A second fragile point, not refuted: every capacity reported is an upper bound on what this model class can reach. The best V step was the last evaluation in 12 of 15 trainings, so longer training or more channels would likely lower all numbers, the per-take ones included.
leads.discriminating_observation: (a) Drive bank against the per-take diagonal. B at G0/G2.5/G5/G7.5/G10: drive bank 0.297/0.350/0.258*/0.329/0.489; per-take models 0.094/0.216/0.260/0.300/0.289. The gap stays at 0.20 at G0 and G10, so the knob is not a pre-model scaling. (b) Level-stratified residual. H5 runs 0.88-0.90 in the quietest input bin against 0.65-0.74 in bins 4-5 at G >= 2.5. With the frozen WH features the bins are 0.315-0.438 at G2.5, 0.225-0.304 at G5* and 0.326-0.380 at G7.5: the quiet-bin excess disappears with a ~13 ms memory static cascade. These features create a quiet-bin excess at G0 (0.469 against 0.31-0.34 in the other bins); the drive bank reduces it only partly (0.421). (c) Transfer matrix: off-diagonal loss grows with gain distance and is uneven. Features from G0 read on G5-G10 give 0.64-0.65; features from G10 read on G2.5-G7.5 give 0.56-0.60. (* = take 20, features trained on it.)

leads.mechanism:
Established, from the JSON, G5 = take 20, fit A, read B.
(1) The prefilter and a saturating static shape together carry the effect. After the 300 Hz high-pass:
- polynomial bases stay high: h5(u)+x 0.792, GMP-aligned 0.695, GMP 0.684;
- every saturating basis lands at 0.61-0.63: tanh+sign 0.634, dvr1 0.632, continuous CPWL 0.628, cpwl_sign 0.628, dvr_static 0.628, DVR with cross terms 0.613, union 0.612, all 0.6125.
- So going from polynomial to saturating after the high-pass is worth -0.16 at G5. Against frozen H5 (0.803) the gain is -0.19.
(2) The RF-specific structure (CPWL knots, DVR types 2-5, GMP lagging and leading envelope terms) adds at most 0.022 beyond tanh+sign. The family is exhausted: all (union + hinges + tanh + sign, 15873 params) equals union (12545 params) within 0.001 at every gain, both A->B and in the in-sample oracle (0.579 vs 0.580).
(3) On raw x, the DVR cross terms act as a crude prefilter: dvr_static 0.784 -> dvr 0.713. After the high-pass they add only 0.015 (0.628 -> 0.613).
(4) The BLA of the take is the wrong prefilter: bla_take union 0.716, tanh 0.748. The tanh value reproduces the scratch study's 0.748.
(5) Parameter count is not what drives the result. hp300 tanh (2305 params, 0.634) beats raw union (12289 params, 0.707). At H5's budget (union with 26 taps, 1275 params) the high-pass still gives 0.707, against 0.803 for H5. Short memory hurts, but the prefilter and shape gain survives.
(6) The level dependence disappears. With the high-pass and any saturating basis, capacity is 0.61-0.65 in every input quintile, against 0.895 -> 0.750 for H5. The extra residual in quiet windows is therefore explained by a static saturating nonlinearity after a fixed high-pass. No dynamic compression is needed to explain it (established on these renders). This matters for lead 4.
Supposed: what remains (about 0.6, level-independent) comes from a prefilter or cascade structure (pre-filter -> clip -> filter -> clip) that one fixed high-pass followed by one static map cannot represent. It does not come from the shape of that map.
leads.discriminating_observation:
Pre-registered criterion: capacity < 0.6 at G5, fit A, ridge chosen off B, read B once.
- Not met. The best A->B value is hp300 union 0.6120 (dvr 0.6132, all 0.6125).
- Only the ORACLE (fitted in-sample on B) crosses the line: all 0.5792, union 0.5798. Correcting for in-sample optimism, p/n = 15873/1.44M ≈ 1.1 % of the residual variance (0.579² = 0.335 → 0.339) gives ≈ 0.582, still below 0.6.
Secondary discriminator (met): the level bins flatten to 0.61-0.65 across all quintiles with the high-pass and saturating bases, against 0.895 → 0.750 for H5.
Control on real hardware (JVM410H OD1 PreampOut, G050): hp300 dvr 0.464, cpwl_sign 0.482, tanh 0.486, against raw h5 0.707. Same pattern: a large gain from shape plus prefilter, ≤ 0.022 from the RF structure.
leads.verdict_reason:
The pre-registered line (< 0.6 at G5, A->B, ridge chosen off B) is not met.
- The best value is 0.6120 (hp300 union), against frozen H5 0.8026 and in-protocol tanh 0.6336.
- The line is crossed only by the ORACLE fitted in-sample on B: 0.5792 for all, 0.5798 for union, about 0.582 after the p/n optimism correction.
- The 0.6 line therefore sits inside the 0.03 gap between oracle and A->B. That gap is a difference of material between A and B (A2 is even harder: 0.673), not missing representation.
Two parts of the hypothesis behave differently:
- Shape after a prefilter matters in one respect: going from polynomial to saturating is worth -0.16 at G5 after the 300 Hz high-pass, -0.17 at G2.5, -0.12 at G0 and -0.13 at G10.
- The RF-PA-specific structure, which is what this lead tests, adds at most 0.022 over a generic tanh+sign basis, and the family saturates (all = union).
The same split appears on the JVM410H hardware: G050 drops 0.707 -> 0.486 with tanh, and DVR adds only 0.022 more.
leads.leakage_and_controls:
How B is kept out of fitting:
- B (di_test) enters a fit only in rows labelled ORACLE (`oracle()`).
- The ridge is chosen on A only: fit on A1 (the first 3/4 of A's blocks), mean residual ratio over the master's targets on A2.
- The A1 and A2 Grams are exact positive semi-definite full-support Grams of the truncated parts (checked against the library). A first run whose part Grams were not positive semi-definite crashed and was discarded.
- The A2 error uses the full-support quadratic form, the library's convention.
- V was not used.

Linearity in y:
- Each prefilter and basis uses one ridge for all of its targets, so fit(y_eval) - fit(y_ref) = fit(d) holds for the published rows.
- h.linearity_check on pair 1->7: hp300 union 4.5e-13, raw union 2.4e-12.
- h.difference_share through the harness reproduces the row share (hp300 union 1->7: 0.82828).

The BLA prefilter:
- The BLA of the take is fitted on all of A to the target. Its output rows are labelled linear_in_target=False, and the A2 selection is not independent of the prefilter (a leak internal to A, labelled).

leads.mechanism:
Supposed (literature, not measured): tube-amp slow states. Grid conduction charges coupling capacitors (blocking distortion, bias shift), the cathode bypass capacitor remembers the bias, the power supply sags (Pakarinen and Yeh 2009). The power amp also has a negative-feedback loop with the presence control. Any of these would make the output depend on input history beyond 5 ms.

Probes tested:
- LPV Hammerstein: each branch x^k is multiplied by z^j (k 1..5, j 0..2, 256 taps each). z is the standardized log of the moving RMS of x over tau = 10 ms to 3 s. Because the features never read y, the probe stays linear in y; linearity gap measured at 1.6e-13 to 3.1e-13.
- Output-level oracle: same features, but z is the level of the true past output, so it reads y on B.
- ARX and polynomial NARX on past outputs.

What was established:
- A history-dependent state exists, and it is not a linear superposition of the previous response.
- It carries little of the output's RMS beyond 30 ms.
- In silence after loud input, the presence-10, gain >= 5 takes decay and then grow again; the plugin answers digital silence with a low-level output after loud input (supposed: an unstable loop).
leads.fragile_hypothesis:
Hypothesis tested: a state or feedback slower than the probe memory carries a large share of the output, so that a probe given history (input envelope, output level, past outputs) would push capacity on B toward 0.3.

Arithmetic requirement (summary.needed_share_for_threshold_0.3): removing a component of relative RMS s lowers capacity by at most s (triangle inequality). Reaching 0.3 therefore needs a mechanism carrying at least H5 - 0.3 of the output RMS: 0.49, 0.50, 0.50 and 0.45 at G2.5, 5, 7.5 and 10, and 0.18 at G0.

leads.limits:
- The LPV family does not resolve a known state. S1 carries 0.11 of its output RMS in the 100-300 ms multisine relaxation and 2.7-3.6 dB of step envelope deviation, yet S1 minus S0 is only 0.010-0.017 at every tau, including 10 ms, where a boxcar cannot track a 0.5 s one-pole. Capacity is second-order insensitive to a component that does not dominate the residual. The LPV results are therefore supporting evidence, not the basis of the refutation.
- The model-free bound comes from controlled transitions: silence into a multisine, and 20 dB steps of Gaussian noise. Applying it to DI playing (plucks, decays) is supposed. Clicks show a larger effect at impulsive onsets (about 0.1 over the first 5 ms).
- All six presence-10, G >= 5 takes are gate-4 excluded. Their self-oscillation sits about 60 dB below the output; its effect during playing is not measured.
- The synthetic devices run at 48 kHz, not 192 kHz.
- Envelope edges: cold start at the beginning of A, and the anticausal envelope zero-filled after the end of B.
- The NARX family is small: lags 2 and 8 linear, lags 2 polynomial of degree 3.
- Runtime about 62 min, slightly over the hour, with nothing dropped.
- A dry run on truncated sections, used only to hunt bugs, is in tmp/probe_capacity/lead5/dryrun.json. It is not a result.

1) Periods 2 and 3 of the multisine differ at -42 dB at G >= 2.5 (-48.9 at G0), against -65.3 for the input and -68.7 for S0. This 0.8% RMS non-periodicity could be time variance or a memory longer than 1 s. It is negligible for capacity but unexplained.
2) What is the hidden click-onset state: bias shift or something else? It persists at 0.5 s and is gone by 1 s, while the output is already at -106 dBFS. Click pairs at varied spacings would measure its time constant.
3) Is the presence-10, G >= 5 regrowth in silence a true self-oscillation (an unstable loop), and is it present during playing?
4) Short-term level used as a feature (10 ms, causal or anticausal) gains about 0.04 at every gain. This points to static scale normalization rather than state; a fixed basis built on x divided by its local RMS could be tested in another lead (supposed).
5) The gap to 0.3 is left to non-state causes, measured elsewhere: filter-nonlinearity cascades and basis shape. A next step would be to decompose the H5 residual by frequency and by harmonic order.

leads.mechanism:
Established on VS100R. The internal states of arm C (pen, blocks) form a basis adapted to the device. A linear readout of that basis represents the FX send far better than the generic bases of the frozen probes, while staying linear in y. The features are taken at the centre knobs (G5 C5, blind to the setting) and fitted on A' (the last 30 s of di_train). On B their residual r/RMS is 0.031-0.044 on the centre and contour takes and 0.25-0.34 at G2.5 and G10. The frozen probes give 0.47-0.77 on the same takes. With features taken at each take's own knobs (setting-aware), the residual is ≤ 0.17 everywhere measured.

Three established controls narrow the mechanism down:
- The untrained random initialisation gives 0.73-0.80 (takes 1 and 9) and 0.49 (take 26), the level of the frozen probes. The gain therefore comes from what the network learned, not from the architecture's dynamics.
- Part of the gain is a linear correction of the model itself. fir_out (a 256-tap FIR on the network output alone) brings take 1 from 0.241 (the raw network) to 0.048. This fits the ~1-sample output delay of arm C measured elsewhere (demo/train_length/predictions.md), but this delay was not measured here.
- At centre knobs the internal features carry more than the output: on take 26, fir_out gives 0.581 against 0.307 for fir_pen and 0.249 for static_blocks; on d01_09, 0.749 against 0.646.

On differences, the features computed at the reference's knobs from x alone act as a model of y_ref. They match or beat the FIR fed the measured y_ref: repeat 0.167 against 0.207 (A'), C10 0.096 against 0.120, G2.5 0.331 against 0.564. Features at the reference's and the evaluated take's knobs side by side ("pair", seed 42) add the gain effect the network learned: G10 drops to 0.122, against 0.646 at centre knobs.

Supposed (not tested): out of domain (Nolly), only a small part of this basis carries over. That would explain why the gain over Hammerstein 5 falls to ~0.1 at G2.5-7.5 and vanishes at G0 and G10.
leads.fragile_hypothesis: The advantage comes from what arm C learned about the device (not from its rich architecture, nor from refitting a model on the targets it was trained on). These frozen features would make a probe basis valid beyond the training device and the training settings.
leads.discriminating_observation:
(1) Untrained random initialisation of the same architecture, setting-blind: take 1 fir_pen 0.748 and static_blocks 0.730; take 9 0.798 and 0.781; take 26 0.486 and 0.479. Trained networks: 0.044, 0.332 and 0.307 (mean over 3 seeds). The cause is learning (established).

(2) Take 16, the only (G, C) pair never trained (takes_same_pair_in_training = 0), behaves like trained take 26 at the same gain: 0.295 against 0.307 at centre knobs, 0.167 against 0.147 at own knobs. The advantage is not limited to the trained settings (established on one take only).

(3) Out of domain (Nolly, level-matched input, centre knobs): fir_pen is 0.666, 0.702 and 0.719 at G2.5, G5 and G7.5, against 0.794, 0.803 and 0.800 for H5. It straddles H5 at G0 (0.488 [0.369-0.575] against 0.476) and at G10 (0.765 [0.717-0.821] against 0.747), and is never near 0.3. On all 19 Nolly differences, the FIR fed the measured y_ref (0.15-0.84) beats the out-of-domain features (0.60-1.01). The basis is mostly specific to its device: the transfer part of the fragile hypothesis is refuted on these data.
leads.verdict_reason: In domain (VS100R), the claim "a linear readout of learned features beats the frozen probes" holds on every take and every difference measured. The margin is large: setting-blind 0.03-0.34 against 0.47-0.77; differences 0.10-0.65 against 0.60-0.95. The random-init control attributes the gain to learning. Out of domain (Nolly), the same features beat H5 only at G2.5-7.5, by about 0.08-0.13, straddle it at G0 and G10, and stay far above the 0.3 threshold. On Nolly differences they are beaten by the FIR fed the measured y_ref. They do not overturn the H2 refusal on Nolly, and they lose the per-branch decomposition.

leads.limits:
**What the readout loses compared with the probes.**
- No decomposition by branch or order (H5 and VL3 split their contributions; here, 16-256 opaque channels).
- It depends on one training run: the spread between seeds is small at the centre (0.042-0.046) but large on take 26 setting-blind (0.245-0.418) and on d01_26 (0.261-0.416).
- It depends on the training data. A metric whose basis comes from arm C would favour models like arm C when scoring models against the device (circularity).
- Exploratory status (D-0010).

**Protocol.**
- A' is 30 s and not the whole of A. The whole-A check on take 1 costs at most 0.04 (static_blocks d01_26 0.237 against 0.275).
- The ridge choice hits the grid edges (1e-8 chosen in the majority, 1 for fir_out), so the readouts are almost unregularised. Out of domain, static pen readouts extrapolate badly: 2.616 at Nolly G2.5 and 2.343 at G10 with gain-matched knobs; 1.321 for one seed at G0; random-init 1.016 on d01_26.
- Level matching on Nolly did not help: the unscaled input (s42) is slightly better. Both are reported and neither was chosen on B.

**Subset (documented).**
- 7 VS100R output takes, 6 differences against take 1.
- "Pair" features: s42 only, gain pairs only (cut during the run, 13-16 min a unit).
- Random control on 3 takes plus Nolly, one draw, no reservoir tuning (spectral radius).
- Nolly gain-matched knobs and unscaled input: s42 only.

**Data.**
- Only one take has a (G, C) pair truly never trained (16). Take 30 shares its pair with take 9, and B/M/T do not reach the FX send.
- One-second input glitches in A' (take 1 at 93 s, take 9 at 105 s).
- The level edges of the stratification differ between VS100R and Nolly (they depend on x).

**Runtime.** About 3 h 15 wall time under shared load, over the ~1 h budget.

**Reading of the raw network.** On Nolly the raw network output is > 1: as a model it is meaningless out of domain.

leads.open_questions:
- When the Nolly arm C (separate queue) exists: does its setting-blind readout fall below 0.3 on the Nolly gain takes? That is the in-domain test that would decide whether a learned basis can carry H2.
- Which share of the in-domain gain is linear correction of the model (delay, post-filter) and which is nonlinear dynamics? fir_out ≈ fir_pen at centre settings, but 0.58 against 0.31 at G2.5 setting-blind. A test that removes the delay (fractional shift) before the readout would separate them.
- Can a usable decomposition be recovered (readout by block, contribution of each block, order of features)?
- Is the edge ridge an artefact of the grid (extend it below 1e-8 and above 1)? A random control with several draws and a tuned reservoir, to rule out a too-weak random basis.
- Fit on the whole of A for every unit (only take 1 / s42 was checked).
- On Nolly, why does the advantage concentrate in the quietest quintile at G5 (0.895 → 0.609) and not at G10 (middle bins worse)? Supposed: tails and compression better carried by the learned basis; not tested.
- Circularity: how would a metric built on an arm-C basis rank arm C against the grey boxes?
